# AI rules — Electron Packaging & Lifecycle (Node/Electron)

Governs `electron-builder.yml`, `scripts/after-pack.js`, `scripts/compress-dmg.js`,
`scripts/build-windows.js`, `scripts/pre-build-check.js`, the `allowScripts` /
`overrides` blocks in `package.json`, and resource-path resolution code in
`src/main/**` (`agent-runner.ts`, `mcp-manager.ts`, `gui-operate-server.ts`,
`sandbox/*-bridge.ts`, `skills-manager.ts`, `index.ts`). See
[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) §3/§6 for the repo layout and dist-\* output
directories.

Packaging uses **electron-builder** (`electron-builder.yml`), not Electron Forge.
There is no separate spawned backend process — the agent engine (`ClaudeAgentRunner`)
runs in-process inside the Electron main process; see [AI_MAIN_PROCESS.md](AI_MAIN_PROCESS.md)
for its internals.

---

## Resource Bundling (`extraResources`)

Each platform (`win`/`mac`/`linux` in `electron-builder.yml`) declares its own
`extraResources` list — they are **not identical**. Before assuming a resource exists
on a given platform, check that platform's block:

| Resource      | win | mac | linux | Purpose                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | --- | --- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mcp/`        | ✅  | ✅  | ✅    | Bundled MCP servers (from `.bundle-resources/mcp`)                                                                                                 |
| `node/`       | ✅  | ✅  | ✅    | Bundled Node runtime, arch-specific dir per platform                                                                                               |
| `python/`     | —   | ✅  | ✅    | Standalone Python (Pillow/pyobjc-Quartz) for GUI automation — **not a spawned backend**, just an interpreter `gui-operate-server.ts` shells out to |
| `tools/`      | —   | ✅  | —     | GUI helper binaries (e.g. `cliclick`) to avoid relying on user-installed Homebrew                                                                  |
| `wsl-agent/`  | ✅  | —   | —     | Compiled sandbox agent for WSL2 (`dist-wsl-agent`)                                                                                                 |
| `lima-agent/` | —   | ✅  | —     | Compiled sandbox agent for Lima (`dist-lima-agent`)                                                                                                |
| `skills/`     | ✅  | ✅  | ✅    | `resources/skills` — extracted (not asar'd) to avoid symlink issues                                                                                |

**Rules:**

- `extraResources` entries land at `process.resourcesPath/<to>` directly — e.g.
  `to: node` → `Contents/Resources/node/` on mac, `resources/node/` on win. Never
  assume an extra `app-resources/`-style subdirectory.
- Always resolve bundled binaries via `process.resourcesPath` at runtime, with a
  dev-mode fallback that walks up from `__dirname`/project root — see the
  `resourcesPath = ... : path.join(process.resourcesPath, 'node')` pattern already
  used in `agent-runner.ts` and `mcp-manager.ts`. Copy that pattern for new bundled
  tools rather than inventing a new resolution strategy.
- Spawned child processes (MCP servers, sandbox agents) do not inherit
  `process.resourcesPath`. Pass it explicitly via env (see
  `env.SQOWE_PILOT_RESOURCES_PATH` in `mcp-manager.ts`) if a spawned process needs it.
- New bundled runtimes/tools require: (1) a `prepare-*.js` script under `scripts/`
  that downloads/stages them into `resources/<name>/<platform>-<arch>/`, (2) an
  `extraResources` entry per platform that needs it, (3) a resolution helper in the
  consuming main-process module.
- `afterPack: ./scripts/after-pack.js` strips binaries and files that don't match
  the build target — koffi platform dirs, better-sqlite3 prebuilds,
  onnxruntime-node's other platforms (plus the duplicate macOS library: npm
  packages hold no symlinks), ngrok binaries, and unused locale files. Each prunes
  only when the target's own file is there. When adding a native
  dependency with per-platform prebuilds, add its pruning logic here or it
  inflates every installer.
- The `files` allowlist in `electron-builder.yml` explicitly lists which
  `node_modules/**` packages ship in the asar. A new runtime dependency with native
  bindings or large payload must be added to this list explicitly — it will NOT be
  included by default just because it's in `package.json` `dependencies`.
- MCP servers are bundled with esbuild (all deps inlined), so the MCP SDK itself
  doesn't need unpacking.

## Window & Menu Lifecycle (macOS + cross-platform)

- On macOS, closing all windows does not quit the app (`app.on('activate')` at
  `src/main/index.ts:1322` recreates the window). Any code holding a
  `BrowserWindow` reference must handle it being destroyed and recreated.
- Never close over a stale `mainWindow` variable in async callbacks or menu handlers
  spanning a window recreation. Guard every access with `mainWindow &&
!mainWindow.isDestroyed()`, or iterate `BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()` when
  broadcasting to all windows (see `emitLocalEmbeddingProgress` in `index.ts` for the
  broadcast pattern).
- `Menu.setApplicationMenu(...)` is called once at startup — do not rebuild the menu
  on window recreate.
- Single-instance lock is `isDev || app.requestSingleInstanceLock()`
  (`src/main/index.ts:337`) so multiple dev windows can run concurrently; do not
  remove the `isDev` bypass.
- **Quitting** (`before-quit` in `index.ts`): the first quit is held back while
  `cleanupSandboxResources()` runs, then `app.quit()` is called again. That second
  call must come from a later task (`setImmediate`): made while Electron is still
  emitting `before-quit`, it is undone when the emit returns (`Browser::Quit`
  assigns `is_quitting_` from it) and the app stays open — Cmd+Q, the Dock's Quit,
  SIGTERM and the quit after a failed start all did, from 2026-03 to 2026-10. And
  the handler must not set `isCleaningUp` itself, or the cleanup skips all its work.

## macOS Entitlements, Signing & GUI Automation

- `NSScreenCaptureUsageDescription` / `NSAccessibilityUsageDescription` in
  `extendInfo` are user-facing permission prompts for `gui-operate-server.ts`
  (vision-based GUI automation) — update the copy there if the automation feature's
  scope changes, never remove the keys while GUI automation ships.
- **Signing.** Releases are built locally with `npm run build`; there is no Apple
  Developer ID. The last step of `scripts/after-pack.js` signs the app with a
  self-signed certificate named `Sqowe Pilot Code Signing` from the login keychain
  (`SQOWE_MAC_SIGN_IDENTITY` overrides the name), through `@electron/osx-sign`,
  with `hardenedRuntime` and the entitlements from `electron-builder.yml` and no
  timestamp. Two reasons:
  - Electron 42+ shows macOS notifications only for a signed app (`UNNotification`).
  - macOS ties screen-recording and accessibility grants to the app's designated
    requirement. The linker signature Electron ships with has the `cdhash` of the
    stock Electron binary: grants survive our releases but reset on every Electron
    upgrade. An ad-hoc signature (`identity: "-"`) seals `Info.plist`, so its
    `cdhash` changes with every release. A certificate's requirement is the bundle
    identifier plus the certificate, the same in every release and Electron version:
    `identifier "com.sqowe.pilot" and certificate root = H"7733de8e…"`. Checked by
    re-signing with only the version changed: new `cdhash`, same requirement.
- The certificate goes to `osx-sign` as its SHA-1 with `identityValidation: false`:
  `osx-sign`'s own lookup lists identities under the basic X.509 policy, where a
  certificate trusted only for code signing does not show ("No identity found").
- electron-builder does not use this certificate: it lists only trusted
  `Developer ID Application:` identities, so `identity: auto` finds none and skips
  signing, and it skips `afterSign` when it did not sign. Signing comes last in
  `after-pack.js` because it seals the bundle — any later change breaks it;
  `compress-dmg.js` packs the signed app afterwards.
- Without the certificate the build goes on unsigned, with a warning; with it, a
  failed signing fails the build. The private key is the app's identity: whoever
  holds it can sign code macOS treats as this app, with its granted permissions.
  It lives in the maintainer's keychain plus an exported `.p12` backup; a new
  certificate means a one-time re-grant for every user.
- Not notarized, so a downloaded copy opens via System Settings → Privacy &
  Security → Open Anyway (macOS 15+ removed the Control-click override).
  Notarization needs a Developer ID; switching to one changes the requirement once.
- Minimum macOS is 13 (Electron 44 dropped macOS 12).

## Native Modules, `allowScripts` & Rebuilds

- **`allowScripts` in `package.json` gates install scripts by EXACT version**
  (`"sharp@0.35.5": true`, …). Bump `sharp`, `onnxruntime-node`, `esbuild`,
  `protobufjs`, or `electron-winstaller` **in the same edit**. Miss it and npm
  reports a single warning among many, the postinstall never runs, and the native
  payload is simply absent — that once left `node_modules/electron/dist/` empty
  and the app would not start.
- `electron` (42+) needs no entry: it has no install script and downloads its
  binary the first time `require('electron')` runs (as `npm run dev` does), into
  `node_modules/electron/dist/`. `npx install-electron --no` fetches it by hand.
- Fixing the entry is not enough: a plain `npm install` does not re-run an install
  script for an already-unpacked package. Follow with `npm rebuild <pkg>`.
- **`npm audit fix --force` is forbidden in this repo.** It ignores `allowScripts`,
  and every remedy it proposes is a downgrade that either fixes nothing or costs a
  feature. CI runs `npm audit --audit-level=critical --omit=dev || true`.
- `sharp` additionally needs an `overrides` entry to move at all — upstream pins
  an older range. Re-check `allowScripts` against installed versions after any
  dependency work; drift there is silent.
- `better-sqlite3` (13+) is an N-API module, so it is not tied to one runtime's
  ABI. Its package carries `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>.node` for every target,
  and `lib/binding.js` loads that file before any `build/` output: one binary
  serves Node (tests) and Electron (app). There is no rebuild step and no
  `allowScripts` entry — the package declares no install script, and its
  `binding.gyp` compiles nothing when a prebuild exists. npm 12 may still list
  "better-sqlite3 (install: node-gyp rebuild)" among blocked scripts (it infers
  one from `binding.gyp`); that is intended — do not allow it. BLOB results come back as copies
  (`Napi::Buffer::Copy`), which Electron's V8 memory cage needs; checked on
  Electron 41.10.7 and 44.9.0 (BLOB round trip, `serialize()`).
- The workflow files install with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`; their
  `npm rebuild better-sqlite3` step is a no-op since 13.
- `npmRebuild: false` in `electron-builder.yml`: no dependency is built against
  Electron's ABI, and `@electron/rebuild` stops the build on any Electron its
  `node-abi` does not know yet — the Electron 44 build failed that way ("Could
  not detect abi for version 44.9.0"). A new ABI-specific native dependency
  means turning it back on and keeping `node-abi` current (an `overrides` entry).

## Native Modules in the Package (`asarUnpack`)

Native binaries can't be loaded from inside the asar, and the wasm files of the
packages below are handled the same way, so each ships in both the `files`
allowlist **and** `asarUnpack`: `better-sqlite3`, `@img`
(sharp), `onnxruntime-node` (`.node`/`.dll`/`.dylib`/`.so`),
`@huggingface/tokenizers` (`.node` + `.wasm`), `@huggingface/transformers`
(`.wasm`), `sharp`, `bufferutil`, `utf-8-validate`, `onnxruntime-web` (`.wasm`).

**One wasm deliberately stays inside the asar:**
`dist-electron/main/photon_rs_bg.wasm`, which pi-coding-agent's image library reads
with `fs.readFileSync` from the main bundle's directory. Electron's asar-aware `fs`
serves that read from inside the archive (checked on Electron 41.10.7), so it needs
neither `asarUnpack` nor a `files` entry beyond `dist-electron/**/*`. The main build
emits it — see [AI_MAIN_PROCESS.md](AI_MAIN_PROCESS.md) §1, "pi is bundled".

**Adding a new native or wasm dependency means updating four places:** the
`files` allowlist, `asarUnpack`, `package.json` `allowScripts`, and
`scripts/after-pack.js` pruning. Miss the last one and every installer carries
binaries for platforms it doesn't target.

## Windows-Specific (NSIS)

- `deleteAppDataOnUninstall: false` is intentional — user config/history/sessions
  persist across uninstall/reinstall. Do not flip this without discussing data
  retention with the user; use explicit in-app cleanup tooling for that instead.
- `signAndEditExecutable: false` — the Windows build is unsigned; do not assume a
  code-signing step exists in `build:win` / `scripts/build-windows.js`.
- `nsis.include: installer.nsh` carries the custom install UI; `oneClick: false`
  and `allowToChangeInstallationDirectory: true` are deliberate.

---

## Common Pitfalls

| Issue                                            | Cause                                                                                    | Rule                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bundled binary not found in packaged app         | Assumed a resource ships on all platforms                                                | Check the platform-specific `extraResources` block before relying on a path                 |
| New dependency missing in packaged app           | Not added to `files` allowlist in `electron-builder.yml`                                 | Explicitly list `node_modules/<pkg>/**/*` for new runtime deps with native code             |
| Native dep's payload missing after a bump        | `allowScripts` keyed on the old exact version                                            | Update `allowScripts` in the same edit as the bump, then `npm rebuild <pkg>`                |
| macOS notifications never show                   | App carries only the linker signature (Electron 42+ needs a signed app)                  | Build where the `Sqowe Pilot Code Signing` certificate is; `after-pack.js` signs with it    |
| Users re-grant screen recording after updates    | Signature without a stable identity — ad-hoc changes per release, linker per Electron    | Sign every release with the same certificate; never switch to `identity: "-"`               |
| Attached images never reach the model            | `photon_rs_bg.wasm` is not next to the main bundle, so pi's image library fails to load  | The main build emits it (`vite.config.ts`); `pre-build-check.js` stops packaging without it |
| Native module loads in dev, fails in the package | Shipped in the asar instead of unpacked                                                  | Add the glob to `asarUnpack` as well as `files`                                             |
| Installer much larger than expected              | No pruning rule in `after-pack.js` for the new native dep                                | Add the pruning logic; mirror the koffi/better-sqlite3/ngrok handling                       |
| Installer carries files of earlier builds        | Main build output not emptied — `vite-plugin-electron` defaults `emptyOutDir` to `false` | Keep `emptyOutDir: true` on the main build in `vite.config.ts`                              |
| Stale `mainWindow` reference after close         | Closure captured `mainWindow` before macOS `activate` recreated it                       | Re-check `!mainWindow.isDestroyed()` at call time, don't cache across awaits                |
| Spawned MCP/sandbox process can't find resources | `process.resourcesPath` is undefined in spawned child processes                          | Pass resource path explicitly via env var to the child process                              |
| SQLite fails to load in the packaged app         | Target's `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>.node` pruned, or not in `asarUnpack`               | Keep `better-sqlite3/**/*.node` in `asarUnpack`; `after-pack.js` prunes only if it exists   |
